root_idea.summary: The lexical field is organized around three recurrent domains: eye disease, ash and ash-like color with associated ruin, and vigorous movement.
root_idea.development: Ashes provide the descriptive basis for ash-colored and finely reduced matter, and for figurative associations with destruction and drought. The evidence also preserves distinct medical and movement branches rather than deriving every usage directly from the noun رَمَاد.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested group is the ordinary noun رَمَاد, normalized from its inflected occurrence رَمَادٍ.

senses.definition: Ashes: burnt charcoal or coals reduced to fine particles and extinguished.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran occurrence, the noun appears in the comparison كَرَمَادٍ, “like ashes,” for material reduced to a barren, insubstantial residue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perish, be destroyed, or become like ashes; also to destroy or reduce a person, thing, or people to such a state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used both intransitively for the subject that perishes and transitively for one who causes destruction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perish through age and wear, becoming worn out and lacking goodness or durability; worn-out or perishing in this condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a garment or other thing that has deteriorated with age.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer from a painful, swollen, inflamed eye or ophthalmia; affected by this eye condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective رَمِد is applied to a person or eye so affected.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause an eye to become painful, swollen, inflamed, or affected with ophthalmia.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use, with the eye as the affected object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put ashes into or upon roast meat, or to put a thing or flesh into live coals; roasted in live coals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active Form II verb describes the cooking action, while مُرَمَّد describes the meat subjected to it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively, to spoil or corrupt a good deed after bringing it into a good state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the proverbial expression for marring a kindness, including by reproaching the recipient or cutting the act short.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a female livestock animal, to show imminent parturition and secrete a small amount of milk in the udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of ewes, goats, she-camels, and cows; the signs may include an enlarged udder, belly, or vulva.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become poor or needy; of a people, to suffer drought, barrenness, or dearth, with resulting loss of cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The poverty use applies to a man, while the drought use applies to a community and its livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man's face, to become ash-colored or to change in appearance through anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IX intransitive description of altered facial color or appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run or move rapidly, vehemently, heedlessly, or headlong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported particularly of a camel and, in some accounts, of an ostrich; the descriptions vary between speed and a random or headlong course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vigorous or energetic going, movement, or action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun denotes energetic activity, and the derived adjective describes one going or acting with energy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, turbid or altered for the worse in taste and color while still drinkable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The condition is associated with water becoming stagnant or otherwise changed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a garment or piece of cloth, faded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use for cloth whose color has deteriorated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ash-color: a color like ashes, dusty and tending toward blackness or dinginess.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A color noun describing an ash-like or dusty hue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ashes that are very fine, abundant, or reduced to the utmost degree of fineness; ashes coming to nothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions emphasize the finely particulate or thoroughly burnt state of the ashes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lye made by infusing wood ashes in water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later technical term for ash-water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person characterized by abundant hospitality and many guests.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiom literally referring to the abundance of cooking-pot ashes produced by frequent cooking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom, to have the face become altered in appearance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression about ashes being blown into someone's face is used figuratively for a changed or disfigured-looking face.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Perdition or destruction; specifically, a year of severe drought and widespread loss.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: عَامُ الرَّمَادَةِ denotes a historically named year of prolonged dearth in which people and livestock perished, or in which the land became ash-like.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A variety of grapes having a dusty black color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional grape designation associated with al-Ta'if.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ash-colored, dusty, or dingy in hue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to ostriches, certain gnats, and garments as well as to other things having a dusky ash-like color.

cautions: The sole Quran occurrence is the noun رَمَادٍ in a comparison, “like ashes”; it does not by itself establish the separate verbal, medical, color, or movement branches documented in Classical Arabic.
